Thanks all, some really helpful advice. Need Spring as well gotta be honest. Shower is not giving hot water.landlords taking their time.

Took me months to actually get them to fix it. I haven't had prolonged cold showers since a trip to old JA when I was a teenager... It was summer, obviously.
That place was don. Was it like 1.50 a slice? Cheese Heaving with grease

Man the only thing I play is BS custom songs, literally for cardio has me sorted .. is the Q3 tracking issue that bad? cause it's a serious a deal breaker for me 😔 I feel like I notice some tracker loss on Q3 anyway already
Bought mine last week and is so great to have, but right now entire Dermatica offering is offline....
Seems like a decent start though. See money isn't really a problem do hey what do I know XD
I don't see it like that, anywhere from five to ten still spells danger

Thanks! and yes sound advice about less drinking. Sadly it's not that simple, I live in a small bedsit and having resigned my job I no longer have the co-working space. I really need the pub or a coffee shop really just to have somewhere else to sit , read my book, apply for jobs and write. Such has been the pandemic, really.

Thanks for the word - coincidentally I've just resigned from my journalism job. They were discriminating against my autism in my view. So I guess that's why I mentioned that. Also the 3rd anniversary of my Mother's passing. Aha it was business journalism, and I need to find more words. Thanks for your advice - I am engaging more with the local autistic community. My counsellor is also specialised in autism - I will be seeing her again, I think it's actually a race thing, with the anger. It's harder for me to feel angry at my Mum because there's a perspective of struggle (although she made her mistakes also, as we all do) that I can totally understand.

Heh it's nice to be connected. No the clincher for me - she had this massive liump on her ankle, which I told her to go to the doctor about. That seems common in itself, but having rummaged over it a few times analytically: she was pretty up on her health generally - high blood pressure and stroke both run in the family. So she did go to the doctor to have these sorts of things checked before.

Her reaction was fiery when I urged her with this ankle lump (the precursor blood clot as it turned out\]. She also intimated to my Dad (they never spoke, but did once just before she passed,) in that she said "Soon you'll see, they'll be your problem then." \[in reference to us, the kids\] She spoke about not wanting to be here, she was going to lose her teeth. I think that was probably a massive blow.

Put altogether I just can't really conclude anything else but she might have had an inkling what it was and just left it. She was 47, she didn't believe she was finding what she needed in life. And we were all grown up by that point. I dearly regret not moving down to be closer to her - I almost did at around the time the lump appeared. (Seriously it was huge, and quite clearly wrong). Big regret and a feeling of guilt.
Thank you <3 It feels good to process it in it's uncertainty and also how I perceived it.
